issue.title: Allow skipping null values for properties handled by `@JsonAnySetter`
`NullPointerException` ("Null 'propertyType' passed") deserializing raw `Map.Entry` with a `Shape.POJO` config override
issue.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched in the [issues](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-databind/issues) and found nothing similar.

### Describe the bug

With the 3.1 `Shape.POJO` support for `Map.Entry` deserialization (#1419) enabled through a config override, reading a raw `Map.Entry` fails with a raw NPE:

```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Null 'propertyType' passed
	at java.base/java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(Objects.java:235)
	at tools.jackson.databind.deser.DeserializerCache.findValueDeserializer(DeserializerCache.java:159)
	at tools.jackson.databind.DeserializationContext.findContextualValueDeserializer(DeserializationContext.java:747)
	at tools.jackson.databind.deser.jdk.MapEntryDeserializer$POJOWrappedDeserializer._createContextual2(MapEntryDeserializer.java:437)
	at tools.jackson.databind.deser.jdk.MapEntryDeserializer$POJOWrappedDeserializer.createContextual(MapEntryDeserializer.java:412)
	...
```

Cause: `POJOWrappedDeserializer._createContextual2()` uses `_valueType.containedTypeOrUnknown(0)` for the key (`MapEntryDeserializer.java:422`) but `_valueType.containedType(1)` for the value (`:435`). For a raw `Map.Entry`, the second call returns `null`. `constructAsPOJO()` (`:125-129`) also skips the "Missing generic type information" check that the natural-shape constructor does (`:60-62`).

With the default shape, the same raw type fails with `InvalidDefinitionException: Missing generic type information for [simple type, class java.util.Map$Entry]`. With `@JsonFormat(shape = POJO)` on a raw `Map.Entry` property, it fails with the same `InvalidDefinitionException`, because the non-contextual default deserializer is built first. So only the type-level config override (or a mix-in) reaches the NPE.

### Version Information

3.x (reproduced on 3.3.0-SNAPSHOT `4f153f0`; the code is unchanged at `33550e9`) and 3.2.4. 2.x does not have `Shape.POJO` deserialization for `Map.Entry`.

### Reproduction

```java
JsonMapper mapper = JsonMapper.builder()
        .withConfigOverride(Map.Entry.class,
                o -> o.setFormat(JsonFormat.Value.forShape(JsonFormat.Shape.POJO)))
        .build();

mapper.readValue("{\"key\":\"a\",\"value\":\"b\"}",
        new TypeReference<Map.Entry<String, String>>() { });   // a=b
mapper.readValue("{\"key\":\"a\",\"value\":\"b\"}", Map.Entry.class);
// NullPointerException: Null 'propertyType' passed
```

### Expected behavior

Either `a=b` with `Object` key/value types, consistent with how the key type is already handled, or an `InvalidDefinitionException` as with the default shape. The NPE should not happen. Using `containedTypeOrUnknown(1)` on line 435 gives the first option. With that change, the full 3.x test suite passes.

### Additional context

This issue was found by an LLM-Enhanced Static Analysis Engine and verified manually.

Per-type `@JsonInclude(NON_DEFAULT)` no longer writes a null over a non-null default, so the null can't round-trip
issue.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched in the [issues](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-databind/issues) and found nothing similar.

### Describe the bug

With `@JsonInclude(NON_DEFAULT)` on a type, a property whose default (from the no-arg constructor) is non-null and which is explicitly set to `null` used to be written as `null`. In 3.2.0 it is omitted, so reading the JSON back restores the default and the `null` is lost.

```java
@JsonInclude(Include.NON_DEFAULT)
public static class Config { public String mode = "default"; }

var mapper = JsonMapper.builder().build();
var c = new Config(); c.mode = null;
mapper.writeValueAsString(c);   // 3.0.4: {"mode":null}   3.2.0: {}
// reading back: 3.0.4 -> null   3.2.0 -> "default"
```

No feature flag is involved. Cause: since #1757, `PropertyBuilder.buildWriter()` sets `suppressNulls = true` in the real-default branch, which is used both for the new global `USE_REAL_INCLUDE_NON_DEFAULT` mode and for the long-standing per-type mode. `JsonInclude1757Test` only pins the global case.

Configuration objects depend on this: `null` is how a default component is switched off, so losing it silently re-enables the default.

Proposal: keep #1757's behavior for the global mode, and restore the pre-3.2 behavior when `NON_DEFAULT` is set per type (annotation or config override). It's a small change in `PropertyBuilder`, with tests, and I'm happy to open a PR against 3.x.

issue.title: Record update with `readerForUpdating()` fails for non-public Record: accessor not made accessible
Current token incorrectly reported when using `@JsonTypeInfo`
issue.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched in the [issues](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-databind/issues) and found nothing similar.

### Describe the bug

A MismatchedInputException gives access to the currentToken of the parser. When using a @JsonTypeInfo with defaultImpl the currentToken without the property is 'END_OBJECT' even if the actual mismatch is at a completely different location and thus token.

### Version Information

Tested the example with 2.21.0, 2.21.5 and 2.22.1

### Reproduction

<-- Any of the following
1. Brief code sample/snippet: include here in preformatted/code section
2. Longer example stored somewhere else (diff repo, snippet), add a link
3. Textual explanation: include here
 -->
I have the following minimal example type ([attached test DefaultImplCurrentTokenTest.java](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29970173/DefaultImplCurrentTokenTest.java))
```java
@JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME, include = JsonTypeInfo.As.PROPERTY, property = "type",
			defaultImpl = Payload.class)
class Payload {
	public int count;
}
```
(Note: The actual use case has a more sensible structure with inheritance and multiple subtypes.)

In all the following cases does it result in a MismatchInputException with message "Cannot deserialize value of type int from String "x": not a valid int value", but the result of getCurrentToken is different.

| Content | getCurrentToken() |
|---------|---------------|
| `{"type":"Payload","count":"x"}` | VALUE_STRING |
| `{"count":"x"}` | END_OBJECT |
| `{"count":"x", "type":"Payload"}` | null |



### Expected behavior

Ideally I would expect that the second case, `{"count": "x"}, would report VALUE_STRING. From #2386 I glance that this is a hard problem. 

Unlike #2386 there may be a backup solution here, returning `null` from `getCurrentToken` has the meaning 'unknown', so that would be a suitable answer.

### Additional context

_No response_

issue.title: `@JsonFormat(shape = ARRAY)` Builder loses property values when not using vanilla processing (e.g. with active View): `deserializeSetAndReturn()` result ignored
`@JsonCreator` for Enums converts value to `String` even if it is not
`ThrowableDeserializer` does not resolve standard `Throwable` property names against `PropertyNamingStrategy`
issue.body:
(generated by Claude code -- apologies for verbosity)
------

`ThrowableDeserializer` matches the standard `Throwable` property names ("message", "localizedMessage", "suppressed", "cause", "stackTrace") against hard-coded canonical names using `equalsIgnoreCase()`. That absorbs case-changing renames, but **cannot** match snake- or kebab-cased ones: `"stack_trace".equalsIgnoreCase("stackTrace")` is `false`. So under such a `PropertyNamingStrategy` the two multi-word names go unrecognized.

This is the unfinished half of #3497 (and follow up to #6157), which was closed after fixing only the `cause` part. `ThrowableDeserializer.construct()` still carries the TODO left at the time:

```java
// 27-May-2022, tatu: TODO -- handle actual renaming of fields to support
//    strategies like kebab- and snake-case where there are changes beyond
//    simple upper-/lower-casing
```

and the read loop repeats the caveat:

```java
// 26-May-2022, tatu: [databind#3497] To support property naming strategies,
//    should ideally mangle property names. But for now let's cheat; works
//    for case-changing although not for kebab/snake cases and "localizedMessage"
```

### Symptoms

All three reproduced on 3.1 (`SNAKE_CASE`, exception with default + single-String constructors):

**1. `localized_message` is reported as an unknown property.** Harmless with 3.x defaults, but with `FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES`:

```
UnrecognizedPropertyException: Unrecognized property "localized_message" ...
  not marked as ignorable (2 known properties: "stack_trace", "cause")
```

The same document with default naming (`localizedMessage`) deserializes fine.

**2. `"stack_trace": null` throws.** `_shouldSkipNullValue()` compares against `"stackTrace"`, so the null is not skipped and reaches `setStackTrace(null)`:

```
NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "[Ljava.lang.StackTraceElement;.clone()" because "stackTrace" is null
```

**3. A view-filtered `stackTrace` is dropped from input.** `_isStandardThrowableProperty()` exempts the standard properties from `@JsonView` filtering by canonical name, so under `SNAKE_CASE` the exemption misses `stack_trace` and the property is skipped — the exception keeps its fill-in trace instead of the one from input. With `FAIL_ON_UNEXPECTED_VIEW_PROPERTIES` this becomes a hard `MismatchedInputException` on well-formed round-tripped output.

Note that symptom 3 is a **regression introduced in 3.1.7 by #6174**; symptoms 1 and 2 are long-standing.

`message`, `cause` and `suppressed` are unaffected in practice — they are single words, so snake/kebab leave them unchanged and `equalsIgnoreCase()` covers `UPPER_CAMEL_CASE`. A *custom* strategy could still rename them, though.

### Suggested fix

Resolve the five external names once, at construction, rather than comparing canonical names at read time. `ThrowableDeserializer.construct()` already receives the `DeserializationContext` and has a single call site in `BeanDeserializerFactory.buildThrowableDeserializer()`, which can pass the `BeanDescription.Supplier`. Each canonical name can then be run through the naming strategy along with its real accessor — found reflectively via `beanDesc.findMethod("setStackTrace", ...)`, `findMethod("initCause", ...)` etc. — exactly the way that method already resolves `cause`:

```java
name = pts.nameForSetterMethod(config, am, "cause");
```

Handing the strategy the actual member (rather than matching accessor names at read time) also keeps custom strategies that inspect the member working.

I have a working patch against 3.1 doing this — ~120 lines including tests covering all three symptoms, each verified to fail beforehand. Happy to open a PR against `3.x`.

### Affects

3.1, 3.2, 3.x (2.x not checked). Targeting `3.x` — too invasive for a patch release.

issue.title: `JsonValueSerializer` re-resolves serializer for every dynamically typed `@JsonValue` result, filling its cache with duplicates
`NullPointerException` when a `@JsonCreator` returns `null` and the input has an Object Id forward reference
`@JsonFilter` with `serializeAllExcept()` does not filter `@JsonAnyGetter` entries
Add lookup-then-resolve helper for dynamic serializers in `StdDynamicSerializer`/`StdContainerSerializer`
issue.body:
### Description

Serializers that resolve value/element serializers dynamically keep a `PropertySerializerMap` (`_dynamicValueSerializers`) and are each expected to hand-write the same two-step sequence:

```java
ValueSerializer<Object> ser = _dynamicValueSerializers.serializerFor(cc);
if (ser == null) {
    if (_valueType.hasGenericTypes()) {
        ser = _findAndAddDynamic(ctxt, ctxt.constructSpecializedType(_valueType, cc));
    } else {
        ser = _findAndAddDynamic(ctxt, cc);
    }
}
```

The shared helpers, `StdDynamicSerializer._findAndAddDynamic()` and `StdContainerSerializer._findAndAddDynamic()`, only do the second step: they never check for an existing entry (nor do `PropertySerializerMap.findAndAdd*()` / `newWith()`). So a caller that forgets the `serializerFor()` check still works, but re-resolves and re-contextualizes the serializer on every call and fills the map with duplicate entries up to its limit of 8.

This has happened at least three times:

- #6392: `JsonValueSerializer` (fixed by #6448)
- #6395: `StdConvertingSerializer`
- #6447: `EnumSetSerializer`

The sequence is currently repeated in (at least) `MapSerializer`, `MapEntrySerializer`, `CollectionSerializer`, `IndexedListSerializer`, `IterableSerializer`, `IteratorSerializer`, `ObjectArraySerializer`, `AsArraySerializerBase`, `ReferenceTypeSerializer` and `JsonValueSerializer`.

### Proposal

Add helper method(s) to `StdDynamicSerializer` and `StdContainerSerializer` that do lookup-then-resolve in one call, something like:

```java
protected final ValueSerializer<Object> _findCachedOrAddDynamic(SerializationContext ctxt,
        JavaType declaredType, Class<?> runtimeType)
```

(plus a variant taking the `UnaryOperator<ValueSerializer<Object>>` transformer for `StdDynamicSerializer`), and convert existing callers to use them, so that omitting the cache lookup is no longer possible by accident.

### Things to consider

- Some callers hold the map in a local variable inside a loop (`CollectionSerializer`, `IndexedListSerializer`) and re-read the field after a miss; the helper should not make these hot loops slower.
- `ReferenceTypeSerializer` and `StdConvertingSerializer` resolve differently on a miss (they do not use `_findAndAddDynamic()`), so may not fit the same helper.
- Callers differ in whether they specialize generic types on a miss; the helper needs to preserve each caller's current behavior.
- Existing `_findAndAddDynamic()` methods are `protected` and may be used by 3rd-party subclasses, so they should be kept (possibly deprecated) rather than changed.
- No behavior change intended; internal refactoring only. Could be done together with, or after, #6395 and #6447.

issue.title: Allow changing serializer used for a single property of a Class
`JsonMapper.builder().filterProvider(...).build()` throws NPE when a `SimpleFilterProvider` has a `null` filter
issue.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched in the [issues](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-databind/issues) and found nothing similar.

### Describe the bug

The Javadoc of `SimpleFilterProvider.addFilter()` says:

> WARNING: Binding `id` or `filter` with `null` value will not be validated within this method, but during serialization of target class annotated with `@JsonFilter`.

That is what happens with `ObjectMapper.writer(FilterProvider)`. The `null` entry is treated as a missing id, so the default filter is used, or a `DatabindException` ("No filter configured with id 'f'") is thrown if there is none. Passing the same provider to the mapper builder instead fails in `build()`, before anything is serialized:

```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "tools.jackson.databind.ser.PropertyFilter.snapshot()" because "v" is null
	at tools.jackson.databind.ser.std.SimpleFilterProvider.lambda$new$0(SimpleFilterProvider.java:68)
	at tools.jackson.databind.ser.std.SimpleFilterProvider.<init>(SimpleFilterProvider.java:68)
	at tools.jackson.databind.ser.std.SimpleFilterProvider.snapshot(SimpleFilterProvider.java:74)
	at tools.jackson.core.util.Snapshottable.takeSnapshot(Snapshottable.java:35)
	at tools.jackson.databind.cfg.MapperBuilderState.<init>(MapperBuilderState.java:182)
	...
	at tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper$Builder.build(JsonMapper.java:45)
```

Cause: the copy constructor used by `snapshot()` calls `v.snapshot()` on every map value (`SimpleFilterProvider.java:68`). The default filter on line 61 uses the null-safe `Snapshottable.takeSnapshot()` instead.

### Version Information

3.x (reproduced on 3.3.0-SNAPSHOT `4f153f0`; the code is unchanged at `33550e9`) and 3.2.4. 2.x does not snapshot filter providers.

### Reproduction

```java
@JsonFilter("f")
static class Bean { public int a = 1; }

SimpleFilterProvider prov = new SimpleFilterProvider()
        .setDefaultFilter(SimpleBeanPropertyFilter.serializeAll())
        .addFilter("f", (SimpleBeanPropertyFilter) null);

new JsonMapper().writer(prov).writeValueAsString(new Bean());   // {"a":1}
JsonMapper.builder().filterProvider(prov).build();              // NullPointerException
```

### Expected behavior

`build()` succeeds and serialization behaves the same as with `writer(prov)`: `{"a":1}` here, or the "No filter configured" `DatabindException` when there is no default filter. A possible fix is `_filtersById.put(k, Snapshottable.takeSnapshot(v))` on line 68. With that change, the full 3.x test suite passes.

### Additional context

This issue was found by an LLM-Enhanced Static Analysis Engine and verified manually.

issue.title: `IllegalArgumentException` thrown by a setter is reported as a type mismatch ("Problem deserializing property ... expected type ... actual type")
Object Ids should NOT be affected by JSON Views or `@JsonFilter`
issue.body:
(note: from #6360) 

Object Ids from `@JsonIdentityInfo` are not regular properties but typically metadata: their visibility and processing should not be affected by regular JSON View (`@JsonView`) processing, or `@JsonFilter` filtering.
Same may be true for type ids (`@JsonTypeInfo`) but that is out-of-scope for this issue.

Let's make sure Object Id reading and writing is orthogonal to View processing.

issue.title: Make `InvokerHolder` access in `AnnotatedConstructor` lazy, to reduce unnecessary eager processing
`@JsonIgnoreProperties`/`@JsonIncludeProperties` not honored for `ObjectNode`/`JsonNode` `@JsonAnyGetter` entries
Vanilla `BeanDeserializer` fast path never used with default settings in 3.x (due to `MapperFeature.DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION` default change)
issue.body:
(filed via Claude Code)

### Describe the bug

In 3.x, the optimized "vanilla" processing of `BeanDeserializer` (`_vanillaDeserialize()`) is never used with default mapper settings -- even for plain POJOs with no `@JsonView` annotations, no injectables, no Object Id and default constructor.

Cause is `BeanDeserializerBuilder._anyViews()`:

```java
protected boolean _anyViews(Collection<SettableBeanProperty> props)
{
    // view processing must be enabled if:
    // (a) fields are not included by default (when deserializing with view), OR
    // (b) one of properties has view(s) to included in defined
    if (!_config.isEnabled(MapperFeature.DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION)) {
        return true;
    }
    ...
```

With `DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION` disabled, every bean deserializer gets `_needViewProcesing = true`, and since `BeanDeserializerBase` computes

```java
_vanillaProcessing = !_nonStandardCreation
        && (_injectables == null)
        && !_needViewProcesing
        && (_objectIdReader == null);
```

`_vanillaProcessing` is always `false`. This logic predates 3.0, when the feature was enabled by default; but #1484 (via #4885) changed the default of `DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION` to `false` for 3.0, so now all POJOs take the non-vanilla `deserializeFromObject()` path regardless of whether views are used at all.

Consequences:

- Default configuration never uses the vanilla fast path, including improvements to it like #6193 (measured about +10% throughput for `byte[]` input -- but only with `DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION` explicitly enabled).
- Afterburner (`SuperSonicBeanDeserializer`, `SuperSonicUnrolledDeserializer`) and Blackbird (`SuperSonicBeanDeserializer`) check `_vanillaProcessing` and fall back to `super.deserialize()` when it is `false`, so their optimized deserialization appears to be bypassed with default settings as well.

### Version Information

3.0.0 and later

### Reproduction

For a plain POJO like

```java
static class Point {
    public int x, y;
}
```

inspecting the root `BeanDeserializer` (e.g. via `DeserializationContext.findRootValueDeserializer()`):

- default `JsonMapper`: `_needViewProcesing = true`, `_vanillaProcessing = false`
- `JsonMapper.builder().enable(MapperFeature.DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION).build()`: `_needViewProcesing = false`, `_vanillaProcessing = true`

(`BeanDeserializerVanillaTest` added by #6193 has to enable `DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION` explicitly to get vanilla processing.)

### Expected behavior

Vanilla processing should be usable whenever no view is active during deserialization (and no other non-vanilla conditions apply). Views only matter if a view is active, and that is already checked at runtime in non-vanilla paths, e.g. `BeanDeserializer`:

```java
if (_needViewProcesing) {
    Class<?> view = ctxt.getActiveView();
    if (view != null) {
        return deserializeWithView(p, ctxt, bean, view);
    }
}
```

Possible approach: stop folding `_needViewProcesing` into `_vanillaProcessing` at construction time, and instead check `!_needViewProcesing || ctxt.getActiveView() == null` at the points where vanilla processing is chosen:

- `BeanDeserializerBase` (flag computation and copy constructors)
- `BeanDeserializer.deserialize()` / `_deserializeOther()`
- `BuilderBasedDeserializer`
- `BeanAsArrayDeserializer` / `BeanAsArrayBuilderDeserializer`
- Afterburner / Blackbird `SuperSonic*` deserializers (jackson-modules-base)

(Note that simply changing `_anyViews()` would not be correct: with `DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION` disabled, an active view excludes un-annotated properties, so view processing is needed whenever a view is active.)

### Additional context

Found while reviewing #6193. Performance difference between vanilla and non-vanilla paths themselves has not yet been measured.

issue.title: `StdConvertingSerializer` looks up and contextualizes delegate serializer for every value when converter output type is dynamic
Property-based creator loop (and vanilla loop after unknown property) silently stop on unexpected token within Object, leaving parser mid-Object
Raw `IllegalArgumentException` escapes polymorphic type-id resolution
issue.body: ## Summary A malformed or conflicting polymorphic type id makes `readValue` throw a raw `IllegalArgumentException` instead of `InvalidTypeIdException`. Code that catches `JacksonException` / `JsonProcessingException` doesn't catch it. ## Details Two calls in `DatabindContext` aren't wrapped: ```java // _resolveAndValidateGeneric, line 269: throws on wrong generic arity JavaType subType = getTypeFactory().constructFromCanonical(subClass); // resolveAndValidateSubType, line 241: throws when the subtype's generic binding conflicts with the base final JavaType subType = getTypeFactory().constructSpecializedType(baseType, cls); ``` The sibling `findClass` call a few lines above is wrapped into `invalidTypeIdException`. These two are not. #1941 and #2668 fixed the same problem for these same methods on other call paths. It happens with a restrictive validator too (`allowIfSubType("java.util.")`). So it doesn't depend on a permissive config like `allowIfBaseType(Object.class)`. ## PoC ```java PolymorphicTypeValidator ptv = BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator.builder() .allowIfSubType("java.util.") .build(); ObjectMapper m = JsonMapper.builder() .activateDefaultTyping(ptv, DefaultTyping.NON_FINAL) .build(); m.readValue("[\"java.util.HashMap\", {}]", Object.class); ``` ``` java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Cannot create TypeBindings for class java.util.HashMap with 1 type parameter: class expects 2 ``` `audit-report/poc/build_exception_leak.sh` runs both sites plus a control (a non-allowlisted type rejected cleanly). ## Impact Low. The exception is thrown before anything is instantiated, so there's no validator bypass and no gadget. In practice: - Spring MVC returns 500 instead of 400 (tested, Spring Boot 3.3.5). - A hand-rolled consumer that only catches `IOException` / `JsonProcessingException` can stall on the record. Spring Kafka's `ErrorHandlingDeserializer` recovers fine (tested, embedded broker). ## Fix Wrap both calls the way #2668 did: ```java try { subType = getTypeFactory().constructFromCanonical(subClass); } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) { throw invalidTypeIdException(baseType, subClass, "problem: (%s) %s".formatted( e.getClass().getName(), ClassUtil.exceptionMessage(e))); } ``` ## References #1941, #2668, #6206

issue.title: Explicit `@JsonView` on a standard `Throwable` property is ignored by `ThrowableDeserializer`
Wrap non-Jackson exceptions from `BeanDeserializerBase.handleUnknownProperty()`
Malformed JSON (or failure) for a single-element container whose only element is filtered with `APPLY_JSON_INCLUDE_FOR_CONTAINERS` + `WRITE_SINGLE_ELEM_ARRAYS_UNWRAPPED`
issue.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched in the [issues](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-databind/issues) and found nothing similar.

### Describe the bug

With `SerializationFeature.APPLY_JSON_INCLUDE_FOR_CONTAINERS` (#5369, #5515) and `SerializationFeature.WRITE_SINGLE_ELEM_ARRAYS_UNWRAPPED` both enabled, a single-element container whose only element is filtered out by `@JsonInclude(content = ...)` produces no value at all: the property name is written without a value.

- If the property is the last one, the output is malformed JSON, e.g. `{"a":1,"v"}`, which `ObjectMapper.readTree()` rejects ("was expecting a colon to separate property name and value").
- If another property follows, serialization fails with `StreamWriteException: Cannot write a property name, expecting a value`.

The decision to unwrap is made from the container size (1) before content filtering is applied (e.g. `IndexedListSerializer.serialize()` checks `len == 1` and then calls `serializeContents()`, which skips the suppressed element). The same happens for `List`, `Set`, other `Collection`s, `String[]` and `Object[]`.

### Version Information

3.x (`3.3.0-SNAPSHOT`, d2d5526).

### Reproduction

```java
public static class L {
    public int a = 1;
    @JsonInclude(content = JsonInclude.Include.NON_EMPTY)
    public List<String> v = new ArrayList<>(List.of(""));
}

JsonMapper m = JsonMapper.builder()
        .enable(SerializationFeature.WRITE_SINGLE_ELEM_ARRAYS_UNWRAPPED,
                SerializationFeature.APPLY_JSON_INCLUDE_FOR_CONTAINERS)
        .build();
m.writeValueAsString(new L());   // {"a":1,"v"}
```

Same output with `Set<String>`, `ArrayDeque<String>`, `String[] {""}` and `Object[] {""}`. Without `WRITE_SINGLE_ELEM_ARRAYS_UNWRAPPED` the result is `{"a":1,"v":[]}`; with two elements (`"x"`, `""`) it is `{"a":1,"v":["x"]}`.

### Expected behavior

Valid JSON. Presumably `{"a":1,"v":[]}` (do not unwrap when no element remains), or omitting the property; which one is preferable is a design choice.

### Additional context

A fix probably needs the single-element check in each container serializer to take filtering into account (e.g. only unwrap when the one element is not suppressed, using the existing `_allElementsSuppressed()` logic), so I have not attached a patch.

This was found while validating an LLM-Enhanced Static Analysis Engine report near this code (`IndexedListSerializer.hasSingleElement`) and verified manually.

issue.title: `MapperFeature.DETECT_PARAMETER_NAMES`=false silently disables `@ConstructorProperties`-based Creator detection too
Global `NON_DEFAULT` with `USE_REAL_INCLUDE_NON_DEFAULT` now writes explicit null` over a non-null default (like per-type); previously nulls were suppressed
issue.body:
Follow-up to #6275 (fixed in PR #6283).

Currently, with `MapperFeature.USE_REAL_INCLUDE_NON_DEFAULT` enabled, global `NON_DEFAULT` (via `changeDefaultPropertyInclusion()`) compares against the real default bean (no-arg constructor) but **always suppresses `null` values** (added for #1757; see `JsonInclude1757Test.testGlobalNonDefaultSuppressesNull`).

Per-type `@JsonInclude(NON_DEFAULT)`, as of the #6275 fix (restoring 3.1.x behavior), instead writes an explicit `null` when the real default is non-null, so that the `null` round-trips. A null real default still suppresses nulls.

So the two modes now differ on null handling, and `MapperFeature.USE_REAL_INCLUDE_NON_DEFAULT` javadoc ("behaves the same as per-class") is no longer accurate.

**Proposal (3.3):** make global real-default `NON_DEFAULT` behave like per-type: do not suppress `null` when the compared default is non-null. This should:
- remove `PropertyBuilder._suppressNullsOnRealDefaults` (added in #6283) and the special-casing;
- flip `testGlobalNonDefaultSuppressesNull` to expect `{"someFieldWithDefault":null}`;
- need a release note, since it changes behavior of an opt-in feature released in 3.2.

Before changing, check the rationale for null suppression in #1757 (reporter @yhack) to make sure it was not a requested behavior.

issue.title: Explicit `JsonFormat.Shape.NUMBER_INT`/`NUMBER_FLOAT` not honored for nanosecond handling of `java.time` values
`Locale` Map keys are still serialized using `Locale.toString()` instead of `Locale.toLanguageTag()`
issue.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched in the [issues](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-databind/issues) and found nothing similar.

### Describe the bug

Jackson 3 changed `Locale` serialization to use BCP-47 language tags (e.g. `en-US`) instead of the legacy `Locale.toString()` representation (e.g. `en_US`).

However, this change does not seem to be applied when a `Locale` is used as a map key.

Serializing a `Locale` directly produces the expected BCP-47 representation:

```json
"en-US"
```

But serializing a `Map<Locale, ?>` still produces the legacy format:

```json
{"en_US":"hello world"}
```

As a result, `Locale` values and `Locale` map keys are serialized differently.

### Version Information

Jackson version: 3.2.4

Java version: 25

### Reproduction

## Reproduction

```java
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Map;

import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

public class Reproducer {
  public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
    JsonMapper mapper = JsonMapper.builder().build();

    String localeJson = mapper.writeValueAsString(
        Locale.forLanguageTag("en-US"));

    String mapJson = mapper.writeValueAsString(
        Map.of(Locale.forLanguageTag("en-US"), "hello world"));

    System.out.println("localeJson = " + localeJson);
    System.out.println("mapJson    = " + mapJson);
  }
}
```

Output:

```text
localeJson = "en-US"
mapJson    = {"en_US":"hello world"}
```

### Expected behavior

`Locale` map keys should be serialized consistently with normal `Locale` values.

Expected output:

```text
localeJson = "en-US"
mapJson    = {"en-US":"hello world"}
```

### Additional context

Locale map key deserialization appears to support both the legacy locale representation (`en_US`) and the BCP-47 representation (`en-US`).

For example, the following JSON deserializes correctly into a `Map<Locale, String>`:

```json
{"en-US":"hello world"}
```

However, serializing a `Map<Locale, String>` still produces:

```json
{"en_US":"hello world"}
```

This means that while deserialization accepts both formats, serialization continues to use the legacy `Locale.toString()` representation for map keys.

I'm not sure whether this is an intentional backward-compatibility decision or an oversight, but I would have expected `Locale` map keys to use the same BCP-47 representation as regular `Locale` values in Jackson 3.

`SerializerCache` read-only lookup is not invalidated when replacing typed serializers
issue.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched in the [issues](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-databind/issues) and found nothing similar.

### Describe the bug

`SerializerCache` maintains `_sharedMap` as the shared serializer cache and `_readOnlyMap` as a derived read-only lookup snapshot used for fast serializer lookups.

The typed serializer registration paths currently invalidate `_readOnlyMap` only when `_sharedMap.put(...)` returns `null`:

```java
if (_sharedMap.put(new TypeKey(type, true), ser) == null) {
    _readOnlyMap.set(null);
}
```

This correctly invalidates the snapshot when a new entry is added.

However, if an existing typed serializer entry is updated, `put(...)` returns the previous serializer rather than `null`, so `_readOnlyMap` is not invalidated.

As a result, `_sharedMap` and `_readOnlyMap` can become inconsistent.

`SerializationContext` instances obtain their read-only lookup from the shared `SerializerCache`:

```java
_knownSerializers = _serializerCache.getReadOnlyLookupMap();
```

If multiple serialization contexts resolve and register a typed serializer for the same key, a later registration can update `_sharedMap` while the cached `_readOnlyMap` snapshot in `SerializerCache` is still considered valid. Subsequent calls to `getReadOnlyLookupMap()` may therefore reuse that stale snapshot instead of creating a new one.

Since `ReadOnlyClassToSerializerMap` returns serializers directly from its snapshot without consulting `_sharedMap`, read-only lookup may continue returning the previously cached serializer.

### Version Information

Current 3.x branch.

### Reproduction

1. Create a `SerializerCache`.
2. Add a typed serializer for a `Class<?>` or `JavaType`.
3. Call `getReadOnlyLookupMap()` to initialize the read-only snapshot.
4. Add another typed serializer for the same key.
5. Call `getReadOnlyLookupMap()` again and query the serializer.


### Expected behavior

The read-only lookup reflects the current serializer stored in `_sharedMap`.

### Additional context

#### Actual behavior

The read-only lookup may continue returning the previously cached serializer because the cached read-only snapshot was not invalidated.

#### Possible fix

Invalidate `_readOnlyMap` whenever a typed serializer entry is added or updated, rather than only when a new key is inserted.

I have a local patch prepared with regression tests covering typed serializer replacement for both `Class<?>` and `JavaType` keys.

issue.title: `@JsonIgnoreProperties` / `@JsonIncludeProperties` not honored on `@JsonAnySetter` properties
Global `NON_DEFAULT` with `USE_REAL_INCLUDE_NON_DEFAULT` skips "empty" check when default bean cannot be created
`@JsonFormat(shape = ARRAY)` deserialization hangs when input ends before `END_ARRAY` while skipping extra values
`EnumSet` serializers re-resolved for every value: dynamic serializer maps never hit for `EnumSet` subclasses
Filter ignored Creator properties at build time instead of per-loop read-time checks
issue.body:
Currently `@JsonIgnoreProperties` / `@JsonIncludeProperties` handling for Creator properties relies on a per-loop read-time guard:

```java
if (IgnorePropertiesUtil.shouldIgnore(propName, _ignorableProps, _includableProps)) {
    handleIgnoredProperty(p, ctxt, handledType(), propName);
    continue;
}
```

placed right after `findCreatorProperty(propName)` resolves a non-null Creator property -- otherwise the by-name ignore check later in the loop is never reached. After #4629 and #6145 (#6146) there are 5 copies of this guard across `BeanDeserializer` and `BuilderBasedDeserializer`, and every new property-based deserialization loop has to remember to add it (#6145 was exactly a case of 3 loops missing it).

### Idea

Filter ignored/non-included names at build time instead: make `PropertyBasedCreator.findCreatorProperty(String)` return `null` for names that should be ignored. Loops would then naturally fall through to the existing by-name ignore handling, and the per-loop guards could be removed. Ignored Creator parameters would simply remain unassigned in `PropertyValueBuffer` (and get default/absent value as now).

### Things to consider

- Ignoral/inclusion sets may differ between contextual variants of the deserializer (`withByNameInclusion()` / `withIgnorableProperties()`), whereas `_propertyBasedCreator` is currently shared; each variant would need its own (filtered) `PropertyBasedCreator` or lookup.
- Other callers of `findCreatorProperty()` (`BeanAsArrayDeserializer`, `MapDeserializer`, `EnumMapDeserializer`, `FactoryBasedEnumDeserializer`) would be affected and need review.
- Behavior with `FAIL_ON_IGNORED_PROPERTIES`, external type id (`ExternalTypeHandler`) and `@JsonUnwrapped` paths must stay as is (covered by existing tests incl. `IgnorePropertiesCreator6145Test`).

Targeting 3.x (not a patch-level change).
